mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% compresses equity discount rates through reduced risk-free rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days. The signal is always active without regime conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% (10th percentile of 2000-2007 data).

mechanism_narrative: A three-month decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% signals labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% in last 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE has fallen below 4.0% in the last 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through revenue acceleration.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and RSAFS growth rates is below 0.3 in the 60-day window prior to the signal, or SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods with strong positive correlation (r>0.5) between HOUST and RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing slowdown and reduced corporate capital expenditure, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines (3-month change < 0).

mechanism_narrative: High employment growth (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs per month consistently supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days without additional conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000 jobs per month (90th percentile of 2000-2007).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained CPIAUCSL annualized growth above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation that triggers monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate decline and employment growth (PAYEMS) indicate labor market tightening that precedes corporate hiring surges and earnings acceleration, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE decline and PAYEMS growth is below 0.4 in the 20-day window prior to the signal, or SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods with strong negative correlation (r < -0.5) between UNRATE and PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, RSAFS growth below GDP growth signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of late-cycle expansion periods when RSAFS growth is below GDP growth (annualized).
